report_name: Windows Botnet x47.c Marketed with 'AI API Drain' Attack Method

threat_actors.name: WraithTools
threat_actors.description: The threat actor selling the x47.c botnet on dark web forums. They market the botnet as a tool to 'eliminate competition' by inflicting financial damage on businesses using AI services.

attack_patterns.name: Cost Harvesting
attack_patterns.description: The x47.c botnet uses stolen API keys to send a high volume of resource-intensive requests to paid AI services like OpenAI, rapidly consuming the victim's prepaid credits or generating large bills. This is referred to as a 'denial of wallet' attack.

attack_patterns.name: Network Denial of Service
attack_patterns.description: The x47.c botnet includes multiple Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attack methods, such as HTTP and UDP floods, as part of its feature set.

attack_patterns.name: External Proxy
attack_patterns.description: x47.c contains a SOCKS5 proxy module to anonymize attacker traffic by routing it through the infected host.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The botnet scans infected Windows systems for sensitive information, including API keys for AI services that are often hardcoded in applications or stored in configuration files.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The botnet is believed to infect systems through common vectors like phishing or malicious downloads.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses
attack_patterns.description: The botnet includes an 'AI Stealth' module which claims to use AI to adapt its concealment techniques on the infected host to evade detection.

malware.name: x47.c
malware.description: A new Windows botnet sold on dark web forums, featuring an 'AI API drain' attack to cause financial harm by abusing victims' AI service API keys. It also includes DDoS, credential theft, and proxy capabilities.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: A provider of paid AI services whose platform is abused by the x47.c botnet to conduct 'denial of wallet' attacks using stolen customer API keys.

identities.name: xAI
identities.description: A provider of paid AI services whose platform is a potential target for abuse by the x47.c botnet, similar to OpenAI.

infrastructure.name: x47.c C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The command and control server infrastructure used by the x47.c botnet to receive stolen API keys and issue commands, including the 'AI API drain' attack.

indicators.name: x47.c Botnet Execution

indicators.name: Anomalous Outbound Connection to OpenAI API
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Outbound Connection to OpenAI API
id: 8b1c2d3e-f4a5-4b6c-7d8e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network connections to the OpenAI API from hosts or processes not expected to use the service. This could indicate a compromised system being used for a 'denial of wallet' attack.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/new-windows-botnet-offers-ai-credit-draining-and-other-attack-methods
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - aml.t0034
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname: 'api.openai.com'
    Initiated: true
  filter_legit_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      # Add other legitimate developer tools or server processes here
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_procs
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to api.openai.com from unexpected hosts, which may indicate an infected botnet node being used for a denial of wallet attack.

indicators.name: Potential API Key Hunting Behavior
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential API Key Hunting Behavior
id: 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-2a3b-4c5d6e7f8a9b
status: experimental
description: Detects processes accessing common configuration files that may contain hardcoded API keys.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/new-windows-botnet-offers-ai-credit-draining-and-other-attack-methods
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.env'
      - 'config.json'
      - 'settings.py'
  filter_legit_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\devenv.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\pycharm64.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_procs
indicators.description: Detects suspicious processes accessing common configuration file types known to store API keys, such as .env or config.json.
